Two of the three fixes look reasonable (adding the >20.0 kg upper-bound rejection, and using `int(total + 0.5)` for round-half-up), but the tier-boundary fix is a red flag.

The agent's own description admits the new logic is asymmetric: the first tier is matched with `weight_kg <= limit` (inclusive), while every other tier is matched with `weight_kg < limit` (exclusive). There's no principled reason given for why the first boundary behaves differently from all the others — the justification offered is essentially "this makes `test_zone2_surcharge_rounds_half_up`/the 2.0 kg case land in the 5.0 kg tier," not a citation of the docstring's actual tier definition. That's the classic pattern of reverse-engineering the implementation from a single failing assertion rather than implementing the rule the docstring actually specifies.

Before merging, someone needs to go back to the docstring's description of the weight tiers (e.g., is each tier defined as "up to X kg" inclusive, or "over prev up to X kg" with a consistent inclusive/exclusive convention?) and implement one consistent boundary rule for *all* tiers that matches that text. If the docstring truly implies inconsistent inclusivity at different boundaries, that should be explicitly quoted in the PR description to justify it — right now the reviewer has no way to verify the fix is correct in general vs. just correct for the specific weights the current tests happen to exercise (e.g., 0.5 kg, 2.0 kg boundaries). As written, this risks silently mis-pricing weights exactly at the untested tier boundaries (5.0, 10.0 kg) since we don't know if they should be inclusive or exclusive either.

Please revise to implement a single, docstring-justified boundary rule (with the rationale spelled out), rather than the current ad hoc first-tier-vs-rest split.
